summary: Assertion signing algorithm mismatch (ES256 vs RS256) causing 403 for private service-to-service calls
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported 403s for scheduled service-to-service calls (batch export job) after an IdP rotation. Failures began after their IdP rotated signing keys and switched assertion tokens to ES256. Our private deployment token verifier appears to reject ES-signed assertions leading to authorization failures at the ingress token-exchange layer.

Impact:
- Arcadian Health: nightly batched exports fail (job retries exhausted).
- Affects service-to-service flows using service-account assertions only in their private VPC deployment.
- Customer-facing data export delayed; manual retries required.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed control plane, v1.14.8 runtime)
- Region: us-east primary; similar failures observed in eu-west replica after failover attempt.

Observed behavior:
- Token introspection returns 401/403 when verifying assertion signature algorithm mismatch.
- Token-verifier logs show expected alg=RS256 but incoming JWT header indicates alg=ES256.

Expected behavior:
- Verify valid signatures for supported algorithms or return explicit guidance to customer.

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Re-issue service-account assertions signed with RS256 OR update private token-verifier to accept ES256.
steps_to_reproduce: Obtain a service-account JWT signed with ES256 from Arcadian's IdP
Submit a token-exchange request to the private control plane token endpoint (POST /v1/token-exchange) with assertion in Assertion param
Observe 403 from ingress-proxy/token-exchange; check token-verifier logs for 'unsupported algorithm' entries
Repeat with RS256-signed assertion to confirm success
logs: 2026-03-10T05:12:09Z ingress-proxy ERROR token-exchange: signature verification failed: unsupported algorithm 'ES256' (expected one of ['RS256'])
token-verifier stack: verify_signature() -> reject: KeyTypeMismatch: expected RSA key for RS256, received EC key
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Asha Patel (Support): Opened with customer-provided logs and sample failing assertion. Customer says rotation was scheduled and they expected backward compatibility.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Priya Rao (SRE): Confirmed unsupported-algorithm error in token-verifier. Private deploy config currently restricts allowed_algorithms to ['RS256'] per security hardening in 1.14.8.
2026-03-10 11:30 - Arcadian Health (Customer): We rolled to ES256 to get smaller token sizes for mobile apps; we did not expect service account tokens to change. Can you advise immediate remediation?

2026-03-10 12:05 - Priya Rao (SRE): Applied temporary config patch on customer's private control plane to add 'ES256' to allowed_algorithms and reloaded token-verifier (hot reload). Confirmed batch job succeeded in test run. Patch noted as temporary; security review required.
2026-03-12 08:20 - Martin Gomez (Security): Requesting follow-up to validate key type handling across JWK sets and to add more explicit error messages for customers when alg mismatch occurs.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: JWKs rotation led to new key type (EC) and algorithm (ES256) which our verifier rejects due to allowed_algorithms config.
Reproduced locally with minimal HTTP client using customer JWT -> token-verifier returns 'KeyTypeMismatch' from underlying crypto library.
Ingress-proxy correctly forwards assertion; failure is in private token-verifier module (auth-service) not in ingress TLS or routing.
Customer's IdP rotation included both RSA and EC keys in their JWKs endpoint but issued ES256 for service-account tokens by default for new service accounts.
Hot-patch (add ES256) resolved customer's immediate outage but flagged by Security team as needing review for policy compliance.
Related to earlier issue SUP-61502 (idp-metadata-fetch-timeout) where stale JWKs can exacerbate signature verification failures under rotation.
No evidence of token tampering; verification failed purely on algorithm/key-type acceptance.
resolution: Workaround applied: temporarily added 'ES256' to allowed_algorithms on the customer's private token-verifier and performed a hot reload; batch jobs resumed. Permanent plan: (1) Security review to approve EC alg acceptance for private deployments, (2) update auth-service to support per-tenant allowed_algorithms with safer defaults and clearer audit logs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/482), (3) ship improved error message with actionable guidance when alg mismatch occurs, (4) create runbook step for IdP rotations. Follow-up task filed: INT-91240 to track deployment-wide config change and policy signoff.
